ib.bias_note: Race 3 has no published start time, so its forecast is read at an estimated 16:30Z first beat. Across a 15:00-17:00Z window the bias only moves between +12.9 and +10.7, so the finding that race 3 is markedly less biased than races 1 and 2 does not depend on that guess.
ib.bias_trend: The bias is not a constant. It ran +19.1, +18.0, +11.2 across the three races — shrinking through the afternoon as the model backed further than the water did. Treat 16 deg as a centre, not a fixed offset, and expect the early races of a day to need the larger correction.

coach.source: Team coach, 9 Sep 2026, with an annotated replay of race 1 (wind label 317°T)
coach.mechanism: The breeze bends against the shoreline. That is what makes the right side mostly the stronger one — and it is the same bend that puts the GRIB 11-19° to the right of reality, because a 7 km grid cell cannot resolve it.
start: Right is stronger, but do not pay for it
Never sacrifice 100–200 m of line bias to get there. A committee-boat start cannot win that back.
If you can see bias, take it
If the bias is visible at all it is probably big enough to be worth more than anything else available on the first beat.
The pin is a long way from the course
The top mark sat above the RC boat, so the pin was about 1 km across the course axis. Starting there only works if you can go right almost immediately.
Nothing on the beat gives it back
What is lost at the gun stays lost. Spend the pre-start gathering clues, not settling.
coach.gate: Gate bias mattered as much as the line. With the left shift at the bottom of the course, the right-hand gate turn came out considerably further upwind.
coach.topmark: A gybe set was the right call — but not from the front pack, where the offset boats throw a lot of dirty air. Spread fleet and more breeze makes it easy; compact fleet and less breeze makes the wind shadow big enough to change the answer.
coach.between: Sail between races. Check wind direction, line bias and top-mark position every time. The biggest decision of the next race is made before the gun, not after it.

daycompare.caveat: Upwind and downwind are split at 8 knots over the whole session, so the slow bucket also holds pre-start manoeuvring and the sail out and back. A longer day therefore drags the "upwind" average down on its own — the downwind and peak figures are the solid ones.
